registered: 2026-11-10, committed before any search below is run

searches.api: GitHub REST code search, GET /search/code?q=QUERY&per_page=100&page=1..10, default sort; raw responses kept locally in bench/out/discovery-h/search
searches.order: repositories in order of their first result; each is looked at in that order
searches.known_limits: code search covers default branches, files under 384 KB and few forks; KiCad 5 projects (.pro) and EasyEDA Pro are not searched

rules: Exclusions, first that applies: the repository, its owner or its fork parent is in a corpus manifest (A to G, P, X) or the November 5 panel (verify.ledger, GitHub fork parent); the repository is named in bench/discovery_p.json, as looked at for the exploratory pilot; a port or copy of an excluded design under another owner, named by hand.

A circuit is: kicad, a .kicad_pro with its root .kicad_sch and a .kicad_pcb in the same folder, its PDF exported by kicad-cli as corpus P's are; eagle, an XML .sch with its schematic PDF; easyeda, a Std schematic JSON with its schematic PDF; altium, a .PcbDoc with its schematic PDF; orcad, an Allegro .brd with its schematic PDF.
A PDF pairs with a source when its name or folder names the same design. Two or more PDFs that could be it, with nothing to say which: excluded, ambiguous pair. Renderings are not collected.
At most two circuits per repository, the first in the order the search listed their files, then by path; at most three per group. Group: the repository owner; known families and ports merge.
Commit: the default branch head when the repository is looked at.
Licence: GitHub's SPDX id; where it is NOASSERTION, the licence file or README read and named; no grant anywhere: none; otherwise not determined, and excluded.
Unavailable (deleted, private, Git LFS pointers, cannot be cloned or built): logged as such, never replaced out of order.

Candidates are pinned in bench/corpus_h.toml, built with build-corpus h, and admitted or not by verify-corpus h --against bench/out/release-2026-11-05/pairs-v2. Quarantined designs stay listed. No extractor runs during discovery.
A generator stops at its 12th admitted design (15 for altium and orcad) in search order, or when its results run out. Designs after the stop leave the manifest and are logged as past the stop.

notes: One circuit per repository (the protocol allows two): decided on 2026-11-10 after screening the first 20 KiCad results and before any build, because the stop counts designs and two per repository would leave about six groups per generator.
A repository in two generators' results is judged once per generator; a circuit taken for one leaves none for the other.

Pairs were judged by hand under the registered rule, with reasons recorded; a name-matching helper only proposed pairs. A display filter hid PDFs whose paths held words such as 'reference'; every exclusion for a missing PDF was then rechecked against the full file list before sealing, which reinstated five OrCAD candidates and corrected two reasons.

Copies of a design already looked at in this discovery, under another owner, are excluded; vendor reference designs and their copies are grouped by vendor (ti, nxp, analog-devices, seeed, littlebits, ataradov).
verify-corpus failed on a top-level folder named 'Eagle Licence'; the licence-file lookup was fixed (no eligibility rule changed) and the corpus re-verified.
Designs whose board KiCad's importer could not open are recorded as not built; the failures repeated on every build.
Code search returns at most 1,000 results per query: 'results exhausted' for OrCAD means those 1,000 (392 repositories).
tjd33/team14 is a TI reference design; corpus F holds a different TI board taken from a third-party copy, so no exclusion rule applies.

A naming clash left one build folder holding another design (pillforge/hardware held PW-Sat2/hardware's files); it was rebuilt from its own repository and re-verified before sealing, and every built published PDF was then checked against its manifest blob (104 of 104 equal). verify-corpus does not itself compare the built PDF with the manifest's blob.

tjd33/team14 was checked against corpus F's TI LAUNCHXL-CC1310 (SWRC319): it is TI's Debug DevPack (SWRC305), a one-page XDS110 debugger board, against a four-page CC1310 LaunchPad; they share no net (net Jaccard 0.0) and only common passive and connector values, though both build TI's XDS110 debugger around a TM4C1294. Kept as a distinct design.

After verify-corpus learned to check builds against the manifest (#12), every design was rebuilt and re-verified on 2026-11-11: all decisions, reasons and content hashes are unchanged; only the 12 KiCad exports' PDF creation times differ, so the seal file was rewritten and its hash in the freeze record updated.
